items.prompt: An order has items worth 20.00 and a 5.00 discount. The user saves with option 12, exits and restarts. What does View order details show?
items.answer: Discount $0.00 and total $20.00, as the reload clamps it before the items return
distractors: Discount $5.00 and total $15.00, as discountAmount is stored in orders.txt
Discount $5.00 and total $20.00, as only the subtotal is recomputed on load
Nothing: the order fails to load and the app starts empty with a warning
items.explanation: The saved discount is read into the Order constructor, which recalculates with no items yet: subtotal 0, so the discount is clamped to 0. Items are restored afterwards. The README does not mention this; verified by saving and reloading in a probe.

items.prompt: An order has a 30.00 pen line and a 5.00 ink line, with a 30.00 discount. The pen line is removed, then three pens are added back. What is the discount now?
items.answer: 5.00, because removing the pen clamped the stored discount to the subtotal
distractors: 30.00, since the clamp limits only the total and leaves the stored discount
0.00, since removing a line from an order clears any discount it carried
The removal is refused while the discount is larger than the new subtotal
items.explanation: recalculateTotals overwrites discountAmount with the subtotal when the discount is larger. After the removal the subtotal is 5.00, so the discount becomes 5.00 and stays there when items come back. Verified in a probe.

items.prompt: Through menu 10, a user applies a 36.00 discount to an order whose subtotal is 35.00. What happens?
items.answer: Refused with "Discount cannot be greater than the order subtotal."
distractors: Accepted and clamped to 35.00, so that the order total becomes 0.00
Accepted as 36.00, which leaves the order total at -1.00
Accepted, and the extra 1.00 is kept as credit for the next item
items.explanation: OrderService.applyDiscount rejects a discount above the subtotal before calling the Order. The clamp the README describes is in Order.recalculateTotals and only matters when the subtotal later drops.

items.prompt: An order is PAID. The user adds another product to it through menu 6. What happens?
items.answer: The item is added and the total rises, as only SHIPPED or CANCELLED block edits
distractors: Refused, since an order can no longer be edited once it has been paid
Refused, since a PAID order has to be moved back to SUBMITTED first
The item is added, and the status drops back to SUBMITTED automatically
items.explanation: isEditable returns false only for SHIPPED and CANCELLED, and addProductToOrder checks nothing else about status. Adding to a paid order changes its total; verified in a probe.

items.prompt: A brand-new DRAFT order has no items. The user moves it to SUBMITTED, then tries PAID. What happens?
items.answer: SUBMITTED succeeds; PAID is refused because the order has no items
distractors: Both are refused, as any status change needs at least one item first
Both succeed, as the empty-order rule applies only to SHIPPED
SUBMITTED is refused, but PAID succeeds since the total is 0.00
items.explanation: DRAFT to SUBMITTED is an allowed transition and the empty-order check covers only PAID and SHIPPED, so the first change works and the second throws "An empty order cannot be moved to PAID."

items.prompt: An order is PAID and the user sets its status to PAID again in menu 11. What does the app print?
items.answer: Could not update order status: Order is already in that status.
distractors: Could not update order status: Invalid status transition from PAID to PAID.
Order status updated. (The status stays PAID and only updatedAt moves.)
Could not update order status: Orders in PAID status cannot be edited.
items.explanation: updateStatus compares the current and new status first and throws "Order is already in that status." before the transition table is consulted.

items.prompt: In menu 11 the user types an order id that does not exist, then the status done. What does the app print?
items.answer: Could not update order status: No enum constant oms.domain.OrderStatus.DONE
distractors: Could not update order status: Order not found.
Invalid menu choice. Please try again.
Could not update order status: Invalid status transition from DRAFT to DONE.
items.explanation: The App upper-cases the text and calls OrderStatus.valueOf before the service looks up the order. valueOf throws IllegalArgumentException with the JDK message, which the catch prints. Verified with piped input.

items.prompt: orders.txt has a line whose status is BOGUS. The user starts the app and at once chooses 13 (Exit). What happens to customers.txt?
items.answer: It is rewritten with just its header line, so every saved customer is gone
distractors: It is left untouched, as exit writes only the files whose data changed
It keeps every customer, as only the orders file failed to load
Nothing: startup aborts with an exception before the menu opens
items.explanation: Any load failure is caught in the App constructor, which prints a warning and starts with empty lists. Exit saves the in-memory state to all four files, so the customers file is overwritten. Verified with a scratch data folder.

items.prompt: A draft order has 2 units of a 10.00 pen. The user adds the same pen again with quantity 1. What does the order hold?
items.answer: One pen line with quantity 3 and a line total of 30.00
distractors: Two pen lines, quantity 2 and 1, adding up to a subtotal of 30.00
One pen line with quantity 1, as adding again replaces the old line
Nothing new: it is refused because the pen is already in the order
items.explanation: addOrMergeItem looks for an existing line with the same productId and increases its quantity instead of adding a second line. Verified in a probe.

items.prompt: Why does OrderItem keep its own productName and unitPrice instead of reading them from the Product?
items.answer: So old orders keep the name and price that held when the line was added
distractors: So the product file can be deleted once every order has been saved
So a product price change reaches every open order automatically
Because Product hides its name and price from classes in other packages
items.explanation: The README calls these fields snapshots: if a product changes later, existing orders still show what was true when the item was added.

items.prompt: In menu 3 a user enters 0.004 as the product price. What happens?
items.answer: Rejected, as it rounds to 0.00 and Product needs a price above zero
distractors: Accepted and stored as 0.004, since BigDecimal keeps every digit typed
Accepted and shown as $0.01, as the price is rounded up to one cent
Rejected with the readMoney hint to enter an amount such as 19.99
items.explanation: readMoney applies setScale(2, HALF_UP), turning 0.004 into 0.00; Product.normalizePrice then throws "Product price must be greater than zero." Verified with piped input.

items.prompt: An order is SHIPPED. addProductToOrder is called on the service with quantity 0. Which error message comes back?
items.answer: Orders in SHIPPED status cannot be edited.
distractors: Quantity must be greater than zero.
Product not found.
Invalid status transition from SHIPPED to DRAFT.
items.explanation: addProductToOrder calls ensureEditable before it checks the quantity or looks up the product, so the status error wins. Verified in a probe.

items.front: List the allowed order status transitions, and where they are defined.
items.back: DRAFT to SUBMITTED or CANCELLED; SUBMITTED to PAID or CANCELLED; PAID to SHIPPED or CANCELLED; nothing out of SHIPPED or CANCELLED. Defined in OrderStatus.allowedTransitions and checked through canTransitionTo.

items.front: Why does this project use BigDecimal instead of double for prices, discounts and totals?
items.back: double is binary floating point, so values like 0.1 + 0.2 do not add up exactly. BigDecimal stores decimal values exactly, which suits money.

items.front: Name the four layers of the order system and what each one holds.
items.back: domain classes represent business concepts; service classes hold business rules; persistence classes save and load; App handles the menu and user input.
